title: profile-scan synthetic regression and threshold oracle
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Deploying new quantization profiles (int8/int4; AWQ/GPTQ variants) causes subtle degradations in output quality that sometimes only appear on narrow cohorts or under specific prompt shapes. Existing eval runs compare point-release metrics but lack a fast, automated way to: 1) scan many profile changes, 2) surface cohort-specific regressions, and 3) synthesize threshold suggestions that are actionable for rollout/rollback policies.

Goal: Build a reproducible 'profile-scan' harness and a lightweight 'threshold-oracle' optimizer that can: run controlled synthetic regressions (perturbations + adversarial examples), rank profiles by risk, propose sensitivity thresholds for automatic rollout gates, and produce human-readable regression summaries for PM/QA/SE teams.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic harness exists that can run N profiles across M cohorts and produce comparable metric vectors (semantic-similarity, perplexity shift, logprob delta, embedding cosine) in <= 6 hours for a 10k sample baseline.

Threshold-oracle suggests numeric thresholds (one per metric) with a recommended rollback policy for each profile; recommendations must reduce false-positive rollbacks on historical data by >= 30% compared to current fixed thresholds.
Generated regression reports include top-10 failing prompts per cohort, example model outputs (float vs quantized), and a one-paragraph human summary suitable for release notes.
Integration tests and a CI job validate harness against two historical incidents, reproducing the earlier detected regressions end-to-end.
Docs and runbook published in Confluence with links to GitHub runner, dashboards, and how-to for using the suggested thresholds in rollouts.
plan: Design: define cohorts (dialogue, code, instruction, long context) and metric slate; finalize synthetic perturbation generators (template swaps, token-drop, paraphrase).
Implement: lightweight runner that accepts a list of model/profile identifiers, sample sets, and metric functions; optimize for parallel execution and streaming metrics back to a time-series store.
Threshold-oracle: implement a bayesian / grid search wrapper that finds threshold points that maximize detection of real regressions while minimizing false alarms on baseline snapshots.
Simulate: run the harness across 12 current quant profiles and two float baselines, analyze drift distributions per-cohort, and produce candidate thresholds.
Validate: replay two historical regression incidents and measure rollback precision/recall; adjust oracle hyperparameters.
Operationalize: add a nightly job, expose report artifact in Console as a link, and document how SRE/PM use thresholds in canary rollouts.
test_plan: Unit tests for metric calculators and deterministic synthetic generators.
Integration test: run harness on small sample against float baseline and one quant profile; check metric deltas are stable across runs.
Regression replay: two archived incidents (INC-2024-05-12, INC-2024-11-02) should be reproduced with similar failure lists.
A/B simulation: feed candidate thresholds into the rollout simulator to estimate expected false rollbacks and missed regressions over 30-day traffic trace.
Load test: confirm harness completes full 10k-sample scan of 12 profiles within 6 hours on a 16-GPU QA cluster.
notes: Design trade-off: heavy-weight, fully randomized adversarial generation gives better coverage but increases runtime. We will start with deterministic template perturbations + lightweight paraphrase models and iterate.
Metrics chosen: embedding cosine, normalized logprob delta, token-level perplexity ratio, and a simple semantic entailment score from the eval-suite.
Cohort definitions seeded from production routing tags + manual sampling from customer-facing flows.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Oracle suggestions overfit to synthetic perturbations and miss real-world regressions. Mitigation: include historical incident replay and sampled production trace in validation.
Risk: Additional CI runtime cost. Mitigation: limit full scans to nightly/weekly and use quick smoke checks for PRs.
Risk: Thresholds differ by cohort causing operational complexity. Mitigation: provide default global thresholds + cohort overrides and a short guide for choosing which to apply.
